g.text: Ninety years of music, 45 places, one city.

text.tspan: Before it was a tech city, Bangalore was Band-galore.
This is the story of how a garden city became India's rock capital: from wartime ballrooms on MG
Road to school bands, smoky cafés, open-air jams in Cubbon Park and stadium gigs at Palace
Grounds. Forty-five places, ninety years, one soundtrack. Start at photo 1 and follow the music.
British-era ballrooms, clubs and theatres, all a short walk apart in
the Cantonment, where dance bands played jazz and swing.
The city's first beat bands grew out of its schools. Duke Ellington
Koshy's, The Only Place and Gaylord: jams, swapped records and
music talk over beers. Cabaret lit up MG Road.
Gigs in Cubbon Park, the free Music Strip stage, and rock pubs like
Freedom Jam, the Strawberry Fields college fest and poolside “rock
happenings” launched a new wave of Bangalore bands.
Deep Purple, the Stones, Iron Maiden and Metallica at Palace
Grounds, Guns N' Roses at Bhartiya City, live music in Indiranagar.
